question: ¿Qué hace drop_na() de tidyterra con un SpatRaster de varias capas y qué hace con un SpatVector? Explica qué ocurre si una celda o geometría tiene un NA en uno de los atributos seleccionados, qué clase devuelve y si puede cambiar la extensión del raster. Cita la documentación.
criteria: Spanish; raster masks cells across layers based on NA in selected layers and trims outer NA cells, so extent can change; vector removes geometries with NA in selected attributes; preserves the respective spatial class; no claim that raster masking returns a tibble or irregular grid; development source links.
answer:
La función `drop_na()` de tidyterra opera de manera diferente dependiendo de si se aplica a un `SpatRaster` o un `SpatVector`.

**Con un SpatRaster:**

Cuando se aplica a un `SpatRaster`, `drop_na()` elimina las celdas que tienen un valor `NA` en cualquiera de las capas seleccionadas. Si no se especifican capas, se consideran todas las capas. Esto significa que si una celda tiene un `NA` en una de las capas, la celda entera se considerará `NA` y se eliminará. 

Además, `drop_na()` también elimina las celdas exteriores que son `NA`, lo que puede cambiar la extensión del raster resultante. Esto se menciona en la [documentación de `drop_na.SpatRaster()`](https://dieghernan.github.io/tidyterra/dev/reference/drop_na.Spat.html), que indica que el método "efectivamente elimina las celdas exteriores que son `NA` (ver `terra::trim()`)".

La clase del objeto devuelto es la misma que la del objeto de entrada, es decir, un `SpatRaster`.

**Con un SpatVector:**

Cuando se aplica a un `SpatVector`, `drop_na()` opera sobre los atributos de las geometrías. Si una geometría tiene un valor `NA` en uno de los atributos seleccionados, la geometría entera se eliminará. 

La [documentación de `drop_na.SpatVector()`](https://dieghernan.github.io/tidyterra/dev/reference/drop_na.Spat.html) indica que el método "opera sobre los atributos, lo que significa que los valores `NA` se evalúan en los atributos (columnas) de cada geometría (fila)". 

La clase del objeto devuelto es la misma que la del objeto de entrada, es decir, un `SpatVector`.

En resumen, `drop_na()` de tidyterra elimina las celdas o geometrías que tienen valores `NA` en los atributos seleccionados, y puede cambiar la extensión del raster si se aplica a un `SpatRaster`. La clase del objeto devuelto es la misma que la del objeto de entrada. 

Esto se puede ver en la [documentación de `drop_na.Spat()`](https://dieghernan.github.io/tidyterra/dev/reference/drop_na.Spat.html) y en los [ejemplos de uso](https://dieghernan.github.io/tidyterra/dev/articles/tidyterra.html).

# S3 method for class 'SpatRaster'
drop_na(data, ...)
```

## Arguments

data

A `SpatVector` created with `[terra::vect()](https://rspatial.github.io/terra/reference/vect.html)` or a `SpatRaster`created with `[terra::rast()](https://rspatial.github.io/terra/reference/rast.html)`.

...

<`[tidy-select](https://tidyr.tidyverse.org/reference/tidyr%5Ftidy%5Fselect.html)`\> Attributes to inspect for missing values. If empty, all attributes are used.

## Value

A `Spat*` object of the same class as `data`. See **Methods**.

## [terra](https://cran.r-project.org/package=terra) equivalent

`[terra::trim()](https://rspatial.github.io/terra/reference/trim.html)`.

## Methods

Implementation of the **generic** `[tidyr::drop_na()](https://tidyr.tidyverse.org/reference/drop%5Fna.html)` methods for `Spat*`objects.

### `[SpatVector](https://rspatial.github.io/terra/reference/vect.html)`

This method operates on attributes, meaning that `NA` values are assessed in the attributes (columns) of each geometry (row). The result is a `[SpatVector](https://rspatial.github.io/terra/reference/vect.html)` with potentially fewer geometries than the input.

### `[SpatRaster](https://rspatial.github.io/terra/reference/rast.html)`

[![[Questioning]](https://dieghernan.github.io/tidyterra/dev/reference/figures/lifecycle-questioning.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#questioning)

The implementation of `drop_na.SpatRaster()` can be understood as a masking method based on the values of the layers (see `[terra::mask()](https://rspatial.github.io/terra/reference/mask.html)`).

`[SpatRaster](https://rspatial.github.io/terra/reference/rast.html)` layers are treated as columns and `SpatRaster`cells as rows, so rows (cells) with any `NA` value on any layer become `NA`. You can also mask the cells (rows) based on the values of specific layers (columns).

`[drop_na()](https://tidyr.tidyverse.org/reference/drop%5Fna.html)` effectively removes outer cells that are `NA` (see `[terra::trim()](https://rspatial.github.io/terra/reference/trim.html)`), so the extent of the resulting object may differ from the extent of the input (see `[terra::resample()](https://rspatial.github.io/terra/reference/resample.html)` for more information).

Check the **Examples** to have a better understanding of this method.

#### Feedback needed!

Visit <https://github.com/dieghernan/tidyterra/issues>. The implementation of this method for `[SpatRaster](https://rspatial.github.io/terra/reference/rast.html)` may change in the future.

## See also

`[tidyr::drop_na()](https://tidyr.tidyverse.org/reference/drop%5Fna.html)`.

Other [tidyr](https://cran.r-project.org/package=tidyr) verbs for handling missing values: `[complete.SpatVector()](https://dieghernan.github.io/tidyterra/dev/reference/complete.SpatVector.html)`, `[expand.SpatVector()](https://dieghernan.github.io/tidyterra/dev/reference/expand.SpatVector.html)`, `[fill.SpatVector()](https://dieghernan.github.io/tidyterra/dev/reference/fill.SpatVector.html)`, `[replace_na.Spat](https://dieghernan.github.io/tidyterra/dev/reference/replace%5Fna.Spat.html)`

## Examples

```

library(terra)

f <- system.file("extdata/cyl.gpkg", package = "tidyterra")

v <- terra::vect(f)

# Add missing values.
v <- v |> mutate(iso2 = ifelse(cpro <= "09", NA, cpro))

# Initial plot.
plot(v, col = "red")


# Drop geometries with missing values in iso2.
v |>
  drop_na(iso2) |>
  plot(col = "red")

# SpatRaster method

# \donttest{
r <- rast(
  crs = "EPSG:3857",
  extent = c(0, 10, 0, 10),
  nlyr = 3,
  resolution = c(2.5, 2.5)
)
terra::values(r) <- seq_len(ncell(r) * nlyr(r))

# Add missing values.
r[r > 13 & r < 22 | r > 31 & r < 45] <- NA

# Initial plot.
plot(r, nc = 3)


# Mask with lyr.1.
r |>
  drop_na(lyr.1) |>
  plot(nc = 3)


# Mask with lyr.2.
r |>
  drop_na(lyr.2) |>
  plot(nc = 3)


# Mask with lyr.3.
r |>
  drop_na(lyr.3) |>
  plot(nc = 3)


# Mask all layers.
r |>
  drop_na() |>
  plot(nc = 3)

# }

# Drop attributes of `Spat*` objects containing missing values

Source: [R/drop-na-Spat.R](https://github.com/dieghernan/tidyterra/blob/main/R/drop-na-Spat.R) 

`drop_na.Spat.Rd`

* `[SpatVector](https://rspatial.github.io/terra/reference/vect.html)`: `[drop_na()](https://tidyr.tidyverse.org/reference/drop%5Fna.html)` drops geometries when any attribute specified by `...` contains a missing value.
* `[SpatRaster](https://rspatial.github.io/terra/reference/rast.html)`: `[drop_na()](https://tidyr.tidyverse.org/reference/drop%5Fna.html)` drops cells when any layer specified by `...` contains a missing value.

## Usage

```
# S3 method for class 'SpatVector'
drop_na(data, ...)

# S3 method for class 'SpatRaster'
drop_na(data, ...)
```

## Arguments

data

A `SpatVector` created with `[terra::vect()](https://rspatial.github.io/terra/reference/vect.html)` or a `SpatRaster`created with `[terra::rast()](https://rspatial.github.io/terra/reference/rast.html)`.

...

<`[tidy-select](https://tidyr.tidyverse.org/reference/tidyr%5Ftidy%5Fselect.html)`\> Attributes to inspect for missing values. If empty, all attributes are used.

## Value

A `Spat*` object of the same class as `data`. See **Methods**.

## [terra](https://cran.r-project.org/package=terra) equivalent

| [tidyr::drop\_na()](https://tidyr.tidyverse.org/reference/drop%5Fna.html)                                                                                     | ✔️                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | ✔️ Remove cell values with NA on any layer and outer cells with NA.                                                                                                                                                    |
| [tidyr::complete()](https://tidyr.tidyverse.org/reference/complete.html)                                                                                      | ✔️                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| [tidyr::expand()](https://tidyr.tidyverse.org/reference/expand.html)                                                                                          | ✔️                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| [tidyr::replace\_na()](https://tidyr.tidyverse.org/reference/replace%5Fna.html)                                                                               | ✔️                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | ✔️                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| [tidyr::fill()](https://tidyr.tidyverse.org/reference/fill.html)                                                                                              | ✔️                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| [tidyr::nest()](https://tidyr.tidyverse.org/reference/nest.html)                                                                                              | ✔️                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

The following sections show some of these methods in action.

### `SpatRaster` objects 

This example uses a `SpatRaster`:

```
library(terra)
f <- system.file("extdata/cyl_temp.tif", package = "tidyterra")

temp <- rast(f)

temp
#> class       : SpatRaster
#> size        : 87, 118, 3  (nrow, ncol, nlyr)
#> resolution  : 3881.255, 3881.255  (x, y)
#> extent      : -612335.4, -154347.3, 4283018, 4620687  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
#> coord. ref. : World_Robinson (ESRI:54030)
#> source      : cyl_temp.tif
#> names       :   tavg_04,   tavg_05,   tavg_06
#> min values  :  1.885463,  5.817587, 10.463377
#> max values  : 13.283829, 16.740898, 21.113781

mod <- temp |>
  select(-1) |>
  mutate(newcol = tavg_06 - tavg_05) |>
  relocate(newcol, .before = 1) |>
  replace_na(list(newcol = 3)) |>
  rename(difference = newcol)

mod
#> class       : SpatRaster
#> size        : 87, 118, 3  (nrow, ncol, nlyr)
#> resolution  : 3881.255, 3881.255  (x, y)
#> extent      : -612335.4, -154347.3, 4283018, 4620687  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
#> coord. ref. : World_Robinson (ESRI:54030)
#> source(s)   : memory
#> names       : difference,   tavg_05,   tavg_06
#> min values  :   2.817647,  5.817587, 10.463377
#> max values  :   5.307511, 16.740898, 21.113781
```

In this example, we:

* Removed the first layer (`tavg_04`).
* Created a new layer `newcol` as the difference between `tavg_06` and `tavg_05`.
* Relocated `newcol` to be the first layer.
* Replaced `NA` values in `newcol` with `3`.
* Renamed `newcol` to `difference`.

Throughout these steps, core properties of the `SpatRaster`, including the number of cells, rows, columns, extent, resolution and CRS, remain unchanged. Other verbs such as `[filter()](https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/reference/filter.html)`, `[slice()](https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/reference/slice.html)` or `[drop_na()](https://tidyr.tidyverse.org/reference/drop%5Fna.html)` may alter these properties in a manner analogous to row operations on data frames.

### `SpatVector` objects 

Most **dplyr** and **tidyr** verbs work with `SpatVector` objects, so you can arrange, group and summarize their attributes.

```
lux <- system.file("ex/lux.shp", package = "terra")

v_lux <- vect(lux)

v_lux |>
  # Create categories.
  mutate(gr = cut(POP / 1000, 5)) |>
  group_by(gr) |>
  # Summarize by group.
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    tot_pop = sum(POP),
    mean_area = mean(AREA)
  ) |>
  # Arrange groups.
  arrange(desc(gr))
#> class       : SpatVector
#> geometry    : polygons
#> dimensions  : 3, 4  (geometries, attributes)
#> extent      : 5.74414, 6.528252, 49.44781, 50.18162  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
#> coord. ref. : lon/lat WGS 84 (EPSG:4326)
#> names       :          gr     n tot_pop mean_area
#> type        :      <fact> <int>   <num>     <num>
#> values      :   (147,183]     2  359427       244
#>               (40.7,76.1]     1   48187       185
#>               (4.99,40.7]     9  194391   209.778
```

The CRS is preserved during these operations. By default, `[summarise()](https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/reference/summarise.html)` merges geometries within each group.

## Plotting with ggplot2 

### `SpatRaster` objects 

When a `SpatRaster` has a CRS defined (`terra::crs(a_rast) != ""`), the geom uses `[ggplot2::coord_sf()](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/ggsf.html)` and can reproject the raster to match other spatial layers.

```
library(ggplot2)

# Facet a SpatRaster object.

ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = temp) +
  facet_wrap(~lyr) +
  scale_fill_whitebox_c(
    palette = "muted",
    na.value = "white"
  )
```
